p.title: Getting Personal: A Deep Learning Artifact for Text-Based Measurement of Personality

ext.title: Getting Personal: A Deep Learning Artifact for Text-Based Measurement of Personality
ext.venue: Information Systems Research, 34(1):194-222 (March 2023; published online 28 March 2022)
ext.document_type: Journal article; design science artifact paper with design evaluation and two forecasting case studies
ext.coverage: Full text read: all lines 1-4297 of C:\Users\pgoff\Documents\research\_text\71f46d6078b0.txt, pp. 194-222 including references. Online Appendices A-I are cited throughout (e.g., Appendix B user-level results, Appendix H COVID-19 case) but are not included in the text file, so those results are not covered. No Paul markup files were specified for this extraction, so paul_markup is empty.
ext.research_question: RQ1: Relative to existing NLP methods, how effectively can DeepPerson detect personality dimensions from user-generated text? RQ2: Can enhanced personality measurement significantly improve downstream forecasting outcomes? (p. 195)
ext.theory: Systemic functional linguistic theory (SFLT; Halliday and Hasan 2004) as kernel theory, with ideational, interpersonal and textual meta-functions mapped to design components (Table 2, p. 201). Big Five (five-factor model; Goldberg 1990) as the personality construct. Psycholinguistic link between psychological states and language (Pennebaker and King 1999). For the downstream case, upper echelons theory (Hambrick 2007) is cited for links between executive traits and firm outcomes. Prediction is framed per Shmueli and Koppius (2011), not causal explanation (p. 196).
ext.data: Design evaluation (Section 4): (1) PANDORA (Reddit), 3,000,566 comments from 1,568 users per the text (Table 3 lists 3,000,068 posts); (2) myPersonality (Facebook), 10,000 status updates from 250 users per the text (Table 3 lists 9,917); (3) Essays, 2,479 essays from 2,479 psychology students (1.9 million words). Labels are survey-based Big Five, median-split to binary per dimension. Splits are 50/25/25 at the user level, repeated 10 times. Pretraining/pseudo-labeling corpora: 1B Word benchmark and Sentiment140 (Go et al. 2009). Downstream case (Section 5): 352 senior executives (219 CEOs, 40 CFOs, 22 CXOs, 188 directors, 62 presidents, 10 chairmen per text; these sum to 541, not reconciled in text) at S&P 1500 firms (425 firms identified), employed 1990-2017 with Twitter accounts; tweets 2006-2017, mean 529 per executive (~186,000 data points); Compustat financials 1990-2017; 519 firm-executive-biennial observations; dependent-variable N ranges 405-519 (Table 10). Unit: user (design eval); firm-executive-two-year period (case study).
ext.method: DeepPerson artifact has three parts: (a) CNN-LSTM encoder: CNN character encoder, word CNN embeddings, two multilayer Bi-LSTMs (ELMo-style, pretrained on 1B Word), one for syntax/semantics and one for LIWC/MRC/SPLICE psychological concept embeddings, aggregated to 1,024-dim (Eqs. 1-3, pp. 200-202); (b) wlpHAN, word-layer-person hierarchical attention with layer attention (Eq. 4), word attention (Eq. 6), and a person-level Bi-LSTM (Eq. 7), softmax over Big Five categories (Eqs. 8-9, pp. 202-204); (c) SPDFiT, self-taught fine-tuning: Bayesian pseudo-labeling with Gaussian class-conditional priors, entropy-based quality score s_m in [0,1] that both filters and scales SGD learning rate (Algorithm 1, p. 206; Section 3.3, pp. 204-206). Implemented on ELMo in PyTorch; mini-batch 500, dropout 0.5, grid search on validation users. Metrics: macro-averaged F, precision, recall, accuracy, AUC; Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Downstream: Big Five scores as features added to baseline features in random forest regression (RFR) and gradient boosted decision trees (GBDT), scikit-learn, 20 estimators; comparators CNN-1, CNN-2, BERT, PersonaBERT, and ARIMA; outcomes measured as the log of the first two-year average after executive entry; improvement = (MSE_baseline - MSE_experimental)/MSE_baseline; Wilcoxon tests (p. 215-216).
ext.identification: None in a causal sense. The authors explicitly frame the downstream test as prediction, not explanation (p. 196, citing Shmueli and Koppius 2011), and acknowledge reverse causality concerns (Hambrick 2007) without resolving them (p. 196). Identification of value is incremental predictive lift: the same RFR/GBDT models are run with and without personality features, with a chronological train/test structure referenced for the main case and a single chronological split reported in Online Appendix G (p. 217). Personality is assumed stable over the analysis period (p. 214, citing Cobb-Clark and Schurer 2012).
ext.scope: Population: social media and essay authors (Reddit, Facebook, psychology students) for detection; S&P 1500 senior executives of US-listed firms for finance forecasting (Section 5). Era: Essays and myPersonality/PANDORA social media data; executive tweets 2006-2017; firm financials 1990-2017; paper published 2022. Institutional setting: IS design science; no institution-level or legislative/lobbying/electoral population is studied in the body text. The COVID-19 case (state and world leaders, Online Appendix H) is referenced but not in the text file. Languages: English implied; not explicitly stated. Nothing in the text addresses lobbying, networks, path-finding, allocation, elections, persuasion, turnout, or legislators, except that Hambrick (2007) is cited for personality being relevant to whether people are elected into leadership roles (p. 196).

key_findings.finding: On PANDORA, DeepPerson reaches AUC 75.0 vs. best comparators AttRCNN 64.6, CNN-1 64.0, PersonaBERT 63.4; macro F 65.1 vs AttRCNN 59.5. Text says DeepPerson beats best comparators by 5-15 pp across measures.
key_findings.numbers: AUC 75.0; Imp. +33.7% vs IBM baseline; AttRCNN AUC 64.6 (+15.2%)

key_findings.finding: On myPersonality, DeepPerson reaches AUC 70.7 vs AttRCNN 63.3 and PersonaBERT 61.2; macro F 67.0 vs 59.0 for AttRCNN. Wilcoxon tests significant (p<0.01) vs CNN-1 on most traits.

SPDFiT is the largest single contributor. Removing wlpHAN drops AUC by about 5 pp. Replacing SPDFiT with UDA, Self-Ensembling, logistic/Lasso/Ridge pseudo-labeling, or BERT variants lowers AUC from 70.0 to 58.3-65.2. Ablation is on PANDORA.
key_findings.numbers: CNN-LSTM (SPDFiT) AUC 70.0 (+20.1%); 1BWord only 62.3; UDA 65.1; Self-Ensembling 65.2; Logistic 64.9; BERT-Base 60.2; PersonaBERT 63.4; Doc2Vec 58.3

key_findings.finding: SPDFiT still beats comparators when only part of the unlabeled data is used: about 50% of unlabeled data gives fairly good results, and SPDFiT outperforms all alternatives at 40%+ of PANDORA or 30%+ of myPersonality unlabeled data.
key_findings.numbers: Unlabeled proportion tested in 10% steps from 10% to 100%

key_findings.finding: wlpHAN outperforms other attention networks. Full wlpHAN AUC 70.3 vs AttRCNN 64.6, HCAN 61.1, HAN 60.7, Msg-Attn 60.5; text reports 3-6 pp lift over those networks and 5-11% relative gains (all p<0.01). Each of the syntax/semantic, concept, and person encoders adds about 2 pp (text claim).
key_findings.numbers: wlpHAN AUC 70.3 (+20.0%); SynSem+Concept+Word 68.0; SynSem+Word 66.2; Word only 64.0 (+9.2%); aspect attention DPA 64.7, CA 63.9, GA 64.8

key_findings.finding: Downstream: adding DeepPerson Big Five scores improves forecasts of firm policy and performance indicators. Average MSE improvement for GBDT is 14.29%, and for RFR 6.67%. Text reports 6.1-14.3% average range across models and MSE/MAE, and 4-15% per variable. Gains for all eight DVs are significant at p<0.05.
key_findings.numbers: GBDT MSE avg +14.29% (CH 20.91, SG&A 31.74, INVEST 11.91, LEVER 12.95, IC 8.65, D&E 8.13, ROA 12.52, CF 7.49); RFR MSE avg +6.67%; GBDT MAE avg +9.46%

key_findings.finding: Comparators add less or nothing downstream. GBDT average MSE improvement: CNN-1 3.38%, BERT 8.62%, CNN-2 -1.80%. ARIMA time-series model is worse, with about 17% higher MSE than GBDT-DeepPerson (ARIMA average -17.05%).
key_findings.numbers: CNN-1 GBDT avg 3.38; BERT GBDT avg 8.62; CNN-2 GBDT avg -1.80; ARIMA GBDT avg -17.05

key_findings.finding: Efficiency claim: DeepPerson uses 800 million pretraining tokens, versus 3.3 billion for BERT-Base and 4.1 billion for PersonaBERT. Authors argue that bigger generic LMs are not enough for personality measurement.
key_findings.numbers: DeepPerson 800M tokens; BERT-Base 3.3B; PersonaBERT 4.1B; RoBERTa about 30B+

key_findings.finding: Error analysis: on instances where DeepPerson most beats comparators, synsem and concept embeddings and SPDFiT yield the largest MSE gains across all five traits. Example concept patterns (LIWC tags such as posemo, anx, work, time) and synsem patterns (POS-tag n-grams) are shown per trait.
key_findings.numbers: 25% of PANDORA instances with widest error margins analyzed per comparator (CNN-1, CNN-2, PersonaBERT, AttRCNN)

key_findings.finding: Design evaluation uses user-level Pearson correlation and MSE to approximate user Big Five scores. Text says DeepPerson is at least 10-18 points higher in correlation and at least 10% lower MSE than the best comparator on PANDORA and myPersonality (user-level results in Online Appendix B, not in text file).
key_findings.numbers: correlation +10-18 points; MSE at least 10% lower

measures: Binary Big Five dimension labels (EXT, NEU, AGR, CON, OPN) from median split of survey scores (p. 206)
Macro-averaged F score, precision, recall, accuracy, AUC; percentage AUC improvement relative to IBM Personality Insights baseline (Tables 4-7)
User-level Pearson correlation and MSE for personality approximation (Appendix B, not in text)
Forecast MSE and MAE percentage improvement relative to a baseline feature set with and without DeepPerson scores (Eq. in p. 216)

Dependent variables from Compustat: investment, cash flow, cash holdings, leverage, interest coverage, SG&A ratio (policy); D&E and ROA (performance); 2-year average of log values after executive entry (Table 10)

Predictors: lagged performance and policy indicators, log total assets, ROA, cash flow, SIC code, executive age, gender, income, education, reputation (count of Google news mentions), LIWC sentiment, LDA top-10 topics, tweet count, followers, favorites (pp. 214-215)
Personality stability assumed over the analysis window (p. 214)
limitations: Authors state: bias is an important consideration for NLP models (Lalor et al. 2022); future work on other languages and on audio and video inputs would be beneficial (p. 219).
Authors state the design evaluation covered only social media posts, forum messages, and essays; speech transcripts and written articles may warrant exploration (p. 219).

Authors acknowledge reverse causality concerns in personality-outcome research (Hambrick 2007) but argue they do not undermine the prediction value of personality measures (p. 196). No causal claims are made.
Authors assume personality is stable over the analysis window, citing Cobb-Clark and Schurer (2012) (p. 214).

Detection model is trained on myPersonality (Facebook) labels and applied to executives' tweets (p. 214). The text reports no validation of executive-level scores against survey measures; user-level validation covers PANDORA and myPersonality only (Appendix B).
Personality labels are binarized by median split for detection (p. 206), so the design evaluation is a binary classification task, not continuous measurement.

Internal inconsistencies in the text: abstract says DeepPerson improves detection by 10-20 pp (p. 194), body says 5-15 pp vs best comparators (p. 209). Text says 3,000,566 Reddit comments and 10,000 Facebook status updates (pp. 205-206), Table 3 lists 3,000,068 posts and 9,917 updates. Executive job-title counts sum to 541 against 352 executives, unreconciled (p. 214).
Downstream sample is 352 executives from 425 firms, with 519 firm-executive-biennial observations; only executives with Twitter accounts were kept, which may not be representative (p. 214).
Essays comparison sample is psychology students (2,479 essays), not executives or public actors.
Appendix results (user-level, robustness, COVID-19 case) are referenced but not in the text file, so they could not be checked here.

short_quotes.quote: DeepPerson can improve detection of personality dimensions by 10–20 percentage points relative to the best comparison methods.
The main commonality between the two being that neither branch generates accurate personality assessments
personality dimensions are significant and powerful predictors of future outcomes with performance/policy implications.
